summary: Defines a SIP header field returned in responses to REGISTER, so a registrar can tell a user agent a service route to use for outbound requests through the registrar's domain. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: When you sign in, the phone system hands you directions on which door to use for calls later. This memo defines that note.

questions: what is the sip service-route header
how does a sip ua learn its service route
what does service-route do in a register response
does service-route apply to incoming sip requests
subtitle: A SIP header that lets a registrar tell a phone which proxies to route its outgoing calls through.

tldr.problem: A SIP user agent that wants outbound services from its home network needs to know which service proxy to use and how to reach it, and that assignment can change dynamically.
tldr.mechanism: The registrar adds a Service-Route header field to its successful REGISTER response. The user agent stores it and may later use it as a preloaded Route header field in its own outgoing initial requests.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3608 is a Proposed Standard. It has since been updated by RFC 5630, and it covers only requests that the user agent originates, not ones sent to it.

today: RFC 3608 is a Proposed Standard and has been updated by RFC 5630. It has not been obsoleted. The text itself says nothing about deployments.

sections.title: The Problem: Finding the Home Service Proxy
sections.content:
The Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) wanted a way to discover home proxies during SIP registration. Its network dynamically assigns a home service proxy to each address-of-record (AOR). That proxy can provide inbound services (for requests terminated at the user agent) and outbound services (for requests the user agent originates).

For inbound requests, the Request-URI matches the AOR, so routing is straightforward. The outbound case raises a question: how does the user agent know which service proxy to use and how to get there?

The RFC lists six alternatives that were discussed: configuration data in the UA, fetching configuration over another protocol such as HTTP, lookup tables in the home network, a 302 response naming the proxy as a new contact, record-routing during REGISTER and reusing that route, and returning the route as a header field in the REGISTER response. It defines the last one. Unlike record-routing, it lets the registrar apply its knowledge of the home network topology when building the route.
sections.eli5: Imagine you move into a new building and need to know which front desk to check in with before making calls. You could have the instructions written into your phone, or look them up every time. This memo picks a simpler way: the front desk just tells you when you sign in.

sections.title: How the Service-Route Mechanism Works
sections.content:
A UA may put a Route header field in an initial request to force it through one or more proxies. Such a route is called a service route or preloaded route. This RFC defines the Service-Route header field to carry one.

The registrar generates a service route for the registering UA and may return it in the response to each successful REGISTER request. The UA can then insert it as a preloaded Route header field in requests it originates. The routing applies only to UA-originated requests, not to requests terminated by that UA.

How the registrar builds the value is local to its implementation and outside the scope of the RFC. The mechanism fits when the registrar knows a service proxy for the UA and has enough knowledge of topology and policy to build a sensible route. It does not support contact-specific routes: the service route is the same for all contacts of one address-of-record.
sections.eli5: When you sign in, the front desk gives you a card listing the stops to make on every outgoing trip. It only helps for trips you start, not for visitors coming to see you.

sections.title: The Service-Route Header Field
sections.content:
The syntax is Service-Route = "Service-Route" HCOLON sr-value *( COMMA sr-value), where sr-value = name-addr *( SEMI rr-param ). Values MUST conform to the syntax of a Route element in the base SIP specification, RFC 3261, and MUST include the loose-routing parameter ;lr for full compliance.

The RFC adds one row to the SIP header usage table: Service-Route appears in 2xx responses, is marked ar in the proxy column, and is optional (o) in REGISTER.
sections.eli5: The note has a fixed format, like an address on an envelope, and every stop on it must be marked as a pass-through stop.

sections.title: Procedures for the UA, Proxy and Registrar
sections.content:
User agent. The UA registers as usual. If the response carries a Service-Route, the UA MAY store it with the address-of-record that was registered. On each refresh, the stored value is replaced by the one in the latest 200-class response. If that response has none, the UA clears the stored route. If a re-registration is refused, or a registration expires and the UA does not re-register, the UA SHOULD discard the stored route. If the UA does use a service route, it uses the content as a preloaded Route in outgoing initial requests and MUST preserve the order.

Proxy. Intermediate proxies treat the field like any unknown header field and forward it. They SHOULD NOT alter it in REGISTER responses, and if they do, the UA MUST NOT be required to accept the change. The RFC gives two reasons: the registrar would lose transparency, and S/MIME protection of the response would make such additions look like a man-in-the-middle alteration. Proxies that insert Record-Route or Path values SHOULD record two route values, one for the receiving interface and one for the sending interface, so routes stay fully invertible.

Registrar. A registrar MAY return one or more Service-Route fields in a 200-class response to a successful REGISTER. Whether to do so and what to put in them is local policy. A REGISTER that only fetches bindings (no Contact header field) SHOULD return the same value as before. If the topology requires a specific proxy first, such as a firewall proxy, the registrar MAY return several entries, visited top-down. The values generally reference only elements within the registrar's own administrative domain.
sections.eli5: The phone keeps the card and swaps it for a new one every time it signs in again. If the new sign-in comes with no card, it throws the old one away. Helpers along the way should pass the card along without scribbling on it.

sections.title: A Worked Example
sections.content:
The RFC's scenario has a user agent UA1 behind a visited proxy P1. The home network has an edge proxy P2, a registrar R, a home service proxy HSP and a database used by both R and HSP. UA1 registers at HOME.EXAMPLE.COM. R is statically configured to reference HSP and knows P2 is the edge proxy, so its 200 response carries a Service-Route of P2 then HSP, each with ;lr. UA1 stores it.

Later UA1 sends an INVITE to UA2 with that value as its Route header field. The service in the example is a logging service that records the call for UA1's user. P1 adds itself to Record-Route. P2 removes itself from the Route and finds HSP by a DNS lookup. HSP executes the service, looks up UA2's contact, removes itself from the Route and sends the INVITE on toward UA2.

UA1 and UA2 are both registered with the same network in this example, but that is not generally required to use a service route.
sections.eli5: You sign in and get a card saying go to the edge desk, then the service desk. When you place a call, it stops at each desk, which makes a note and passes it along until it reaches your friend.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Proxies between the UA and the registrar could change the returned Service-Route, or insert one when the registrar sent none. The consequence is that later requests might be diverted to or through an unintended node. Proxies on the INVITE path could mount many other attacks.

Systems using Service-Route SHOULD provide hop-by-hop message integrity and mutual authentication, and UAs SHOULD request it with a sips: URI. Registrars returning a Service-Route MUST implement end-to-end protection using S/MIME and SHOULD use it for all such responses. UAs SHOULD authenticate attached S/MIME bodies if present.
sections.eli5: If someone sneaks a fake card into your hand, your calls could be sent to the wrong place. So the front desk should seal the card, and you should check the seal.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: The RFC defines the SIP extension header field Service-Route, which has been included in the registry of SIP header fields defined in RFC 3261. The SIP change process, RFC 3427, requires general SIP extension header fields to be defined by a standards-track RFC, and this document supplies that definition. The registration lists the RFC number 3608, the field name Service-Route and no compact form.
sections.eli5: The new note type gets written into the official list of SIP note types so nobody else uses the same name.
